Jordan — great questions. Answers below and a proposed test configuration attached. Short version first, details after.

Quick answers:
- Default rate limits (hosted API): 100 RPS per API key by default; adjustable via support for higher tiers. Per-tenant sustained limits can be set for Dedicated pools.
- Burst model: token-bucket style with short-term burst allowance (up to 500 RPS for <60s) depending on plan and provisioning; sustained throttling applies if average over a minute exceeds quota.
- Failover: hosted API is region-aware and will route to nearest healthy region; Dedicated supports active-passive with warm standbys by default; active-active can be configured for enterprise customers with cross-region warm pools and sticky KV caches. In practice we do smart routing + short KV cache rebuilds to minimize cold-start latencies.
- Error budget policy: for Dedicated we publish a 99.95% uptime SLA with a 0.05% monthly error budget; hosted default is 99.9%. When error budgets are exceeded we follow an escalation policy — first alerting and throttling of non-critical routes, then automatic fallback to compatible smaller model variants or read-only cached responses depending on the route. We do not silently drop requests; failure modes are 429 (rate limit) or 503 (service degraded) with clear headers and retry-after guidance.

Suggested test details (attached in test-config.yaml):
- 24–48h total run, with three 10–15m burst windows each day (up to 300 RPS) and a sustained baseline matching your expected production profile.
- Monitor for 429 vs 503 breakdown, p50/p95/p99 latency, and KV cache-miss rate during failover.
- We’ll provide a temporary dedicated test pool for ACME: 4 GPUs, reserved for the 48h window, with cross-region warm standby enabled for one failover test.

I’ve provisioned a short-lived API key (ACME-TEST-KEY) and attached the test-config. I’ll also open a HubSpot task under deal RD-2026-ACME-47 with the provisioning details: https://hubspot.com/deal/RD-2026-ACME-47

Attachment: test-config.yaml
